summary: Jonathan Geen is an indologist and scholar of religious studies who earned his doctorate from McMaster University under Phyllis Granoff by 2001. He has held teaching posts at McMaster University, Butler University, and the University of Rochester.

Jonathan Glover is a philosopher who studied at Tonbridge School (~1954–1959) and Corpus Christi College, Oxford (~1960–1964). He held a post at King's College London (~1998–2013) and taught Amber D. Carpenter.

Jonathan Lear (1948–2025) was a philosopher who studied at Yale (~1966–1970), Cambridge (~1970–1973), and Rockefeller University (~1973–1978). He taught Amber D. Carpenter and held a post at the University of Chicago (~1996–2025).

Jonathan Mark Kenoyer is a historian, archaeologist, and indologist educated at Woodstock School and the University of California, Berkeley (~1970–1983). He has served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison since circa 1985.

Jonathan Z. Smith (1938–2017) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Haverford College, Yale Divinity School, and Yale University. He held posts at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1966–1968) and the University of Chicago (~1968–2013).

Jong-Nam Choi is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Shitennoji University and completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg in 1998 under Lambert Schmithausen, also studying under Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan, Albrecht Wezler, and David Seyfort Ruegg.

Jongcheol Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Seoul National University and earned his PhD at the University of Tokyo (1994). He held posts at the University of Mysore (1992) and the Academy of Korean Studies (2001).

Jongmyung Kim works in Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and religious studies. Educated at Yonsei University, Seoul National University, and UCLA (MA, 1994), he served as Associate Professor of Korean Buddhism at the Academy of Korean Studies (attested 2012–2019).
Joryu Chiba (1921–2008) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Ryukoku University from circa 1941 to 1944 and later served there as a professor from circa 1968 to 1992.

Josef Schick (1859–1944) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Albrecht Weber (~1880–1882). He held academic posts at Heidelberg University (~1889–1896) and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1896–1926).

Joseph Campbell (1904–1987) was a religious studies scholar educated at Canterbury School, Dartmouth, Columbia, Paris, and Munich. He taught at Canterbury School (1933–1934) and Sarah Lawrence College (1934–1972).
Joseph D. Markowski is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his Master of Arts at McGill University under the supervision of G. Victor Sōgen Hori (attested 2004).

Joseph E. Schwartzberg (1928–2018) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Brooklyn College (~1945–1949). He served as Professor of geography at the University of Minnesota from circa 1964 until 2018.

Joseph Goldstein is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who attended Columbia University (~1961–1965). He studied under Anagarika Munindra and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, and taught Jon Kabat-Zinn.

Joseph Hackin (1886–1941) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Central Asia, and Buddhism. Educated in Paris, he held posts at the Musée Guimet (1913–1941), the French Archeological Delegation to Afghanistan (~1923–1940), and the EPHE (~1928–1940).

Joseph John Loizzo is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar educated at Amherst College and Harvard University, where he studied under Robert A. F. Thurman. He founded the Nalanda Institute and was a Visiting Scholar at Columbia University (attested 2007).
Joseph Margolis (1924–2021) was a philosopher who studied at Columbia University (~1947–1953). He taught at Temple University (~1968–2021) and instructed Youru Wang.

Joseph Marino is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his PhD at the University of Washington (attested 2017), where he studied under doctoral supervisor Richard Salomon and teacher Collett Cox.

Joseph Mitsuo Kitagawa (1915–1992) was a religious studies and Japanology scholar. Educated at Rikkyo University and the University of Chicago (PhD 1951), he held posts at Chicago (~1951–1985; attested Dean 1988) and taught Reginald Ray, Catherine Bell, and Rita Gross.

Joseph Prabhu is a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He held an associate professorship at California State University, Los Angeles (attested 1989, 2007) and visiting posts at United Theological College, UC Santa Barbara, and Bossey Ecumenical Institute.
